sources.entry: TablePro - Fast database client with AI-assisted SQL editing and support for major SQL/NoSQL engines. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/datlechin/TablePro) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: TablePro is a free, open-source, native database client for macOS and iOS that connects to major SQL and NoSQL engines, with built-in AI chat and SQL assistance.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a native database client built without Electron, JDBC, or a JavaScript runtime, using native drivers for major SQL and NoSQL databases. It offers an SQL editor with autocomplete, multi-cursor, and Vim mode, plus a data grid with inline editing, sorting, filtering, and undo/redo. It supports native window tabs, multi-window, split panes, SSH tunnels (password or key auth), and SSL/TLS. Query history has full-text search. AI features include chat, inline suggestions, Explain/Optimize, and an MCP server so tools like Cursor, Raycast, or Claude Desktop can query databases; users can bring their own API key or run local models with Ollama. A plugin system lets users write their own drivers in Swift, and plugin drivers install on demand.
use_cases: Browse and edit data in MySQL, PostgreSQL, or other SQL databases
Query NoSQL databases from a native Mac app
Write and optimize SQL with AI assistance
Connect to remote databases through SSH tunnels
Let AI coding or chat tools access a local database via MCP
Use a free alternative to TablePlus on macOS
how_to_run: Or download the app from GitHub Releases
To build from source: brew install xcodegen
Open TablePro.xcodeproj in Xcode 26+ or build with xcodebuild (see README)
notable: Native apps with no Electron, JDBC, or JavaScript runtime
Multi-database support in a native macOS client, positioned against single-engine and Electron-based clients
Built-in AI chat, inline suggestions, and MCP server, with BYO API key or local Ollama
Swift plugin system for writing custom database drivers
Free to use on every database; paid license adds extra Mac features
caveats: Linux version is in development and not released; Windows is not supported
Several advanced features (iCloud Sync, Team Library, Data Rewind, etc.) require a paid Starter or Team license on Mac
Building from source requires Xcode 26 or later and XcodeGen
